newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index drops 2.37 pct, breaks support.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index drops 2.37 pct, breaks support.

text.p: Philippine shares fell further at midsession on Wednesday as it fell through a support level due to lingering concerns over the local currency, brokers said.

"People are very negative about the equities market. This short-term uncertainty about the peso, whether it will be devalued or not, has changed our view on the market giving the bearish scenario greater weight," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
The main index fell 64.03 points in midtrade to 2,634.63.
Blue chip issues were seen dragging the main index down in midtrade.
They were Philippine Long Distance Telephone Co, Metrobank, Meralco B, Piltel, Ayala Land Inc and Petron Corp.
"It's difficult to defuse the situation involving the peso. The stock market is suffering because of it," said Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities.

The Central Bank had to sell dollars heavily in early Wednesday trade as the market reacted to a report by the Singapore Straits Times which reported Trade Secretary Cesar Bautista as saying that the devaluation of the peso would be discussed at today's Monetary Board meeting.
The Board is the policy-making arm of the Central Bank.
Bautista and Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson denied that peso devaluation was part of the agenda.
The Philippine composite index broke through the 2,650 support in midsession and traders said that if it breaks the 2,600 major support, the market may touch its lows in May.
In May, the market was battered by fears of a property crash and talks that the Philippines was going to suffer a financial crisis similar to Thailand.
